regimens.indication: Acute Bacterial Meningitis (S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, H. influenzae) — Adults

refs.quote: Meningitis Caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Neisseria meningitidis or Streptococcus pneumoniae .
In the treatment of meningitis, it is recommended that the initial therapeutic dose be 100 mg/kg (not to exceed 4 grams).

dose.frequency: every 12 hours (total 4 g/day) infused over 30 minutes for 7 to 14 days

regimens.dose_text: In bacterial meningitis, initial dose 100 mg/kg (up to 4 g), then 2 g IV every 12 hours (4 g/day total) infused over 30 minutes for 7 to 14 days. Do not administer simultaneously with calcium-containing IV solutions.

refs.quote: Meningitis Caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Neisseria meningitidis or Streptococcus pneumoniae .

In the treatment of meningitis, it is recommended that the initial therapeutic dose be 100 mg/kg (not to exceed 4 grams). Thereafter, a total daily dose of 100 mg/kg/day (not to exceed 4 grams daily) is recommended. The daily dose may be administered once a day (or in equally divided doses every 12 hours). The usual duration of therapy is 7 to 14 days.

dose.frequency: once daily or divided every 12 hours (50 mg/kg q12h) for 7 to 14 days

regimens.dose_text: Initial therapeutic dose 100 mg/kg IV (not to exceed 4 g), followed by 100 mg/kg/day (not to exceed 4 g/day) once daily or divided every 12 hours for 7 to 14 days. Administer over 30 minutes (60 minutes in term neonates).

regimens.indication: Lower Respiratory Tract, Skin/Skin Structure, UTI, Pelvic Inflammatory Disease, Bacterial Septicemia, Bone/Joint, and Intra-Abdominal Infections — Adults (IV)

refs.quote: Ceftriaxone for injection, USP is indicated for the treatment of the following infections when caused by susceptible organisms: Lower Respiratory Tract Infections
The usual adult daily dose is 1 to 2 grams given once a day (or in equally divided doses twice a day) depending on the type and severity of infection. The total daily dose should not exceed 4 grams.

dose.frequency: once daily (1 to 2 g/day once daily or divided twice daily; max 4 g/day)

regimens.dose_text: 1 to 2 g IV once daily (or in equally divided doses twice daily) over 30 minutes, depending on type and severity of infection; total daily dose not to exceed 4 g. Usual duration 4 to 14 days (at least 10 days for S. pyogenes).

regimens.indication: Lower Respiratory Tract, Skin/Skin Structure, UTI, Pelvic Inflammatory Disease, Bacterial Septicemia, Bone/Joint, and Intra-Abdominal Infections — Adults (IM)

refs.quote: Ceftriaxone may be administered intravenously or intramuscularly.
The usual adult daily dose is 1 to 2 grams given once a day (or in equally divided doses twice a day) depending on the type and severity of infection. The total daily dose should not exceed 4 grams.

dose.frequency: once daily (1 to 2 g/day once daily or divided twice daily; max 4 g/day)

regimens.dose_text: 1 to 2 g deep IM once daily (or in equally divided doses twice daily); total daily dose not to exceed 4 g. Usual duration 4 to 14 days.

regimens.indication: Uncomplicated Gonococcal Infections (Cervical/Urethral, Rectal, Pharyngeal) — Adults

refs.quote: Uncomplicated Gonorrhea (cervical/urethral and rectal) Caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae , including both penicillinase- and nonpenicillinase-producing strains, and pharyngeal gonorrhea caused by nonpenicillinase-producing strains of Neisseria gonorrhoeae .
For the treatment of uncomplicated gonococcal infections, a single intramuscular dose of 250 mg is recommended.

regimens.dose_text: Single intramuscular dose of 250 mg. Add appropriate antichlamydial coverage if Chlamydia trachomatis is suspected.

refs.quote: Surgical Prophylaxis The preoperative administration of a single 1 g dose of ceftriaxone may reduce the incidence of postoperative infections in patients undergoing surgical procedures classified as contaminated or potentially contaminated
For preoperative use (surgical prophylaxis), a single dose of 1 gram administered intravenously 1/2 to 2 hours before surgery is recommended.

dose.frequency: single IV dose 0.5 to 2 hours before surgery

regimens.dose_text: Single 1 g IV dose administered 1/2 to 2 hours before surgery.

regimens.indication: Skin and Skin Structure Infections — Pediatrics

refs.quote: For the treatment of skin and skin structure infections, the recommended total daily dose is 50 to 75 mg/kg given once a day (or in equally divided doses twice a day). The total daily dose should not exceed 2 grams.

dose.frequency: once daily or divided twice daily (50 to 75 mg/kg/day; max 2 g/day)

regimens.dose_text: 50 to 75 mg/kg/day IV (or IM) once daily or in equally divided doses twice daily; total daily dose should not exceed 2 g.

regimens.indication: Serious Miscellaneous Infections Other Than Meningitis — Pediatrics

refs.quote: For the treatment of serious miscellaneous infections other than meningitis, the recommended total daily dose is 50 to 75 mg/kg, given in divided doses every 12 hours. The total daily dose should not exceed 2 grams.

dose.frequency: total daily dose (50 to 75 mg/kg/day) given in divided doses every 12 hours (max 2 g/day)

regimens.dose_text: 50 to 75 mg/kg/day IV (or IM) given in divided doses every 12 hours; total daily dose should not exceed 2 g.

refs.quote: Acute Bacterial Otitis Media Caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae (including beta-lactamase producing strains) or Moraxella catarrhalis (including beta-lactamase producing strains).
For the treatment of acute bacterial otitis media, a single intramuscular dose of 50 mg/kg (not to exceed 1 gram) is recommended (see INDICATIONS AND USAGE ).

regimens.dose_text: Single intramuscular dose of 50 mg/kg (not to exceed 1 g).

regimens.indication: Susceptible Infections — Term Neonates (<= 28 days, Non-Hyperbilirubinemic, No Calcium IV Solutions)

refs.quote: Ceftriaxone is contraindicated in premature neonates (see CONTRAINDICATIONS ). Ceftriaxone is contraindicated in neonates (≤ 28 days) if they require (or are expected to require) treatment with calcium-containing IV solutions, including continuous calcium-containing infusions such as parenteral nutrition because of the risk of precipitation of ceftriaxone-calcium
Intravenous doses should be given over 60 minutes in neonates to reduce the risk of bilirubin encephalopathy.

regimens.dose_text: Administer IV doses over 60 minutes in neonates to reduce the risk of bilirubin encephalopathy. Contraindicated in premature neonates (<= 41 weeks PMA), hyperbilirubinemic neonates, and neonates (<= 28 days) requiring calcium-containing IV solutions.

value.drug_or_class: Calcium-Containing IV Solutions and Diluents (Ringer's, Hartmann's, Parenteral Nutrition)
value.effect: Incompatibility causing precipitation of insoluble ceftriaxone-calcium salt crystals; cases of fatal crystalline precipitation in lungs and kidneys of neonates.
value.management: Do not use calcium-containing diluents for reconstitution or infusion lines; in non-neonates, sequential administration requires thorough flushing with compatible fluid.

refs.quote: Do not use diluents containing calcium, such as Ringer’s solution or Hartmann’s solution, to reconstitute ceftriaxone vials or to further dilute a reconstituted vial for IV administration because a precipitate can form. Precipitation of ceftriaxone-calcium can also occur when ceftriaxone is mixed with calcium-containing solutions in the same IV administration line.
